does.method: Update: clean-up of last frame's requests
does.text: At the top of each update the system destroys every entity on which ecl::tutorial::FinishResetResetTutorialsProcessOneFrameComponent was added, and further down every entity on which ecl::tutorial::ResetProfileOneFrameComponent or ecl::tutorial::ShowResetMessageRequestOneFrameComponent was added. The destroys go through the deferred command buffer, so they remove the carrier entities this system created on the previous pass; the components never outlive a frame.
does.evidence: EoCClient.dll+0x63BD50 ecl::tutorial::ResetSystem::Update: first Added/Alive query on spec DAT_181a04ae8 (resolved through its init to GetTypeName: FinishResetResetTutorialsProcessOneFrameComponent, Added) with DestroyEntity per entity; third Added/Alive query on spec DAT_181a04b0c (ResetProfileOneFrame, ShowResetMessageRequestOneFrame) with DestroyEntity per entity, issued after the creates of this pass in the same deferred buffer.
does.review: Review 2026-11-14 (Opus): the earlier 'not checkable live: gone is judged against the holders before the recipe' misread the verb: gone also passes for an entity that came to hold the type inside the recipe and then stopped (cli.md 3.6, Prelude.lua); so the claim is given appears-as-E plus gone-on-E. The finish marker is used because it is created whether or not a profile had tutorials shown.

does.text: The system walks the notification entities that hold eoc::notification::ResetTutorialsMessageRequestNotificationComponent and ecl::notification::AcceptedComponent (ecl::notification::SeenComponent is in the query's second type list; its role was not settled). For a notification whose UserId's low half is 1, whose high half matches the default user id's high half, and that resolves to a non-empty profile GUID, it reads ecl::splitscreen::PlayersSingletonComponent; if the singleton is there, for Player1 (when its id is non-zero) and for Player2 (when its id is non-zero and the notification's byte field_4 is 0) it marks that a reset was processed and looks the player's profile up. If that profile has any tutorial entry shown (net::PlayerProfile::HasAnyTutorialEntryShown): with field_4 = 0 the profile GUID is collected for a profile reset; with field_4 non-zero the player's id is collected for a reset message.
does.evidence: EoCClient.dll+0x63BD50 ecl::tutorial::ResetSystem::Update: Persistent/Alive query on spec DAT_181a04aec (TL<ResetTutorialsMessageRequestNotification, Accepted>, TL<Seen>); the test (short)UserId == 1, PlayerManager::GetDefaultUserId / GetPlayerProfileGUID, the -1 test on the GUID, FUN_18063b240 (only user of the WorldView string, reads the splitscreen singleton), the reads at Player1+4 and Player2+4 (0x1c), the profile lookup through the manager's virtual slot 0x100, HasAnyTutorialEntryShown, and the branch on the byte at notification+4 between two collecting calls (FUN_1805a1de0 for the GUID set, FUN_18054ed60 for the player-id set).

does.method: Update: creates the profile reset requests
does.text: After the walk, for every collected profile GUID the system creates a new entity and adds ecl::tutorial::ResetProfileOneFrameComponent holding that GUID (ProfileGuid). So the component appears, on the client, in the frame after the player accepts a Reset Tutorials notification whose field_4 is 0 while the local profile has seen at least one tutorial.

does.method: Update: creates the reset message requests
does.text: For every collected player id the system creates an entity with ecl::tutorial::ShowResetMessageRequestOneFrameComponent holding that id (PlayerId). This happens instead of the profile reset when the accepted notification's field_4 is non-zero (and only for Player1, since Player2 is considered only when field_4 is 0).
